subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: Should OpenClaw make reliable project/task memory a default core behavior, document it as a workspace/plugin pattern, or split this umbrella into narrower memory engine and session-recall fixes first?
rationale: Current main has partial opt-in primitives, but there is no established default project/task state contract and broader recall has privacy and product-boundary tradeoffs automation should not choose.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

options.title: Route to recall proposals
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99611 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51386 as the primary product path for cross-session recall, leaving this issue only for project/task mutation semantics.

options.title: Document a workspace/plugin pattern
options.body: If default task memory should stay outside core, convert the request into a documented reliability pack or plugin pattern instead of adding more core behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The open maintainer-labeled same-assistant recall proposal already frames the core privacy and product-direction choice for the cross-session recall slice.
